title: A Lake with Too Many Good Intentions
passage:
A small lake outside Kawaoka became popular after photos of its clear water spread online. Visitors came to walk, take pictures, and feed ducks near the shore. Local businesses welcomed the attention because more people bought food and rented bicycles. Within a year, however, park staff noticed cloudy water near the feeding area and an unusual increase in algae.

Many visitors believed feeding ducks was kind. They brought bread, rice, and snacks, sometimes in large bags. Environmental researchers explained that ducks naturally eat a varied diet and that large amounts of human food changed both their behavior and the lake. Uneaten food sank, adding nutrients to the water. More ducks also remained in one area because food was easy to obtain, increasing waste in the same place.

The town first placed signs saying ‘Do Not Feed the Ducks.’ The signs gave no explanation. Some visitors obeyed, but others thought the rule was unnecessarily strict and continued feeding when staff were not nearby. A few people even argued online that the town was preventing children from enjoying nature.

The park changed its approach. New signs explained the chain of effects with simple pictures: extra food, more nutrients, more algae, less oxygen in the water. The signs also suggested alternatives such as quietly watching birds, using binoculars, or joining a monthly nature walk. Staff stopped describing feeders as irresponsible and instead emphasized that many people fed ducks because they cared about them.

At the same time, the town worked with nearby cafés. Shops stopped selling bags of old bread marketed for ducks. One café created a small bird-observation card for children, with spaces to mark different behaviors such as swimming, cleaning feathers, or searching for natural food. Children who completed the card received a sticker.

After one season, feeding decreased noticeably, although it did not disappear. Water quality near the shore improved slightly, but researchers warned that weather and other factors also affected algae, so the improvement could not be credited to one action alone. The town continued monitoring the lake rather than declaring the problem solved.

The experience revealed a difficult type of environmental problem: harm can come from behavior motivated by kindness. Simply accusing people of not caring would have misunderstood the situation. The more effective response was to explain how a caring action could produce an unwanted result and to offer another way to express the same interest in animals. The lake project reminded residents that good intentions matter, but intentions do not guarantee good outcomes. Caring responsibly sometimes requires changing what we do after learning more about the system we are trying to help.
translation:
川岡の郊外にある小さな湖は、透明な水の写真がインターネットで広まり人気になりました。散歩や写真撮影、岸辺のカモへの餌やりを楽しむ人が増え、地域の店も歓迎していました。しかし一年ほどすると、餌やり場所の水が濁り、藻が増えていることが分かりました。

多くの人はカモに餌をあげることを親切だと考え、パンや米、お菓子などを大量に持ってきました。研究者によると、食べ残しは水底に沈み栄養分を増やし、藻の増加につながります。また簡単に餌が得られるためカモが同じ場所へ集中し、排せつ物も増えます。

町は最初『餌を与えないでください』という看板だけを設置しました。しかし理由が書かれていなかったため、厳しすぎる規則だと感じる人もおり、職員がいないと餌を与える人がいました。子どもが自然を楽しむ機会を奪うという批判も出ました。

そこで新しい看板では『余分な餌→水中の栄養増加→藻の増加→酸素減少』というつながりを絵で説明し、双眼鏡で観察する、自然観察会へ参加するなど代わりの楽しみ方も示しました。餌を与える人を無責任と決めつけず、多くは動物を大切に思っていることも認めました。

近くのカフェとも協力し、カモ用として古いパンを販売するのをやめました。ある店は子ども向けに、泳ぐ、羽づくろいする、自然の餌を探すなどの行動を観察するカードを作り、完成するとシールを渡しました。

一季節後、餌やりは明らかに減りました。岸辺の水質にも少し改善が見られましたが、研究者は天候など他の要因もあるため、一つの対策だけの成果とは言えないと注意しました。町は監視を続けています。

この経験は、善意から始まった行動でも環境へ害を与えることがあるという難しさを示しました。『自然を大切にしていない』と責めるだけでは状況を誤解します。善意の行動がなぜ望ましくない結果につながるか説明し、動物への関心を別の形で表す方法を示す方が効果的でした。良い意図は重要ですが、それだけで良い結果が保証されるわけではありません。
